_about: The ten case types: the cards on /find-lawyers, the list on the home page and the national guide pages (/family-lawyers ...). Plain, general, evergreen information only: no fees, deadlines or figures, and nothing that depends on a single state unless it says so. Built by scripts/build-case-pages.mjs.

family.name: Family Law & Divorce
family.h1: Family Law & Divorce Lawyers in the United States
family.card: Divorce, child custody, support and dividing property.
family.description: When to hire a family lawyer, what they do and what to ask. Then find family law firms by state and city.
family.lede: A family lawyer helps with the legal side of separation and divorce: where the children will live and how decisions about them are made, child support and spousal support (alimony), and how property and debts are divided. Many also draft prenuptial and postnuptial agreements and parenting plans, so arrangements are clear before a dispute starts.
when: You are separating, or thinking about it, and want to understand your rights before you act.
You and your spouse need to settle custody, parenting time, support or who keeps the home.
You have been served with divorce papers or handed a proposed settlement and are unsure what to sign.
You want a prenuptial or postnuptial agreement.
An existing order no longer fits because income, work or living arrangements have changed.
does: Explains your rights and options under your state's family law.
Negotiates a settlement agreement, or represents you in mediation or collaborative divorce.
Prepares court filings and appears for you if the case cannot be settled.
Helps with financial disclosure, the records both sides must exchange.
Drafts or reviews prenuptial agreements and parenting plans.
family.differ: Family law is mostly state law. Each state sets its own rules on how long you must live there before filing, how property is divided (some states use community property, others equitable distribution), and how custody and support are decided. The same facts can lead to different results in different states, so hire someone who practices family law in your state.
ask: How much of your practice is family law, and have you handled cases like mine?
Do you recommend mediation or a negotiated settlement before going to court?
How do you bill, what retainer do you require, and what is billed separately?
What should I do, and not do, before we speak again?

faqs.q: Do I need a lawyer to get a divorce?
faqs.a: You are not required to hire one, and some people complete an uncontested divorce on their own. A lawyer is worth considering when there are children, property, retirement accounts or a business involved, or when you and your spouse disagree, because agreements you sign can be hard to change later.

faqs.q: What is the difference between mediation and going to court?
faqs.a: In mediation a neutral person helps the two of you reach an agreement that you control. In court a judge decides if you cannot agree. Many lawyers try to settle first because it is usually faster and less adversarial, and court remains available if it is needed.

faqs.q: Can a custody or support order be changed later?
faqs.a: Often yes, when circumstances have changed in a meaningful way, such as a change in income or in a child's needs. A lawyer can tell you whether your situation meets the standard that applies in your state.

faqs.q: How do I find a family lawyer near me?
faqs.a: Choose your state or city on this page to see the family law firms LawDB lists there, with their addresses, phone numbers and the practice areas they handle.

criminal.name: Criminal Defense
criminal.h1: Criminal Defense Lawyers in the United States
criminal.card: Arrests, criminal charges and DUI, from the first hours on.
criminal.description: When to hire a criminal defense lawyer, what they do and what to ask. Then find criminal defense firms by state and city.
criminal.lede: A criminal defense lawyer represents people who have been arrested or charged with a crime, from DUI and drug charges to theft, assault and serious felonies. They explain the charges and your rights, deal with the prosecutor, and defend you in court if the case goes to trial. The earlier a lawyer is involved, the more options there usually are.
when: You have been arrested, charged or told you are under investigation.
Police want to question you, or you have received a court date or summons.
You were charged with DUI or another driving offense and your license is at risk.
You want to know whether a past record can be sealed or expunged.
You are a non-citizen and a charge could affect your immigration status.
does: Explains the charges, the possible outcomes and your rights.
Speaks with the police and the prosecutor on your behalf.
Challenges the evidence and negotiates, where appropriate, for a reduced charge or dismissal.
Represents you at hearings, at trial and at sentencing.
Advises on bail, probation and sealing or expunging a record.
criminal.differ: Criminal law is mostly state law, with its own offenses, courts and procedures in each state, and federal charges are handled in separate federal courts. Rules on DUI penalties, bail and record sealing differ a lot from state to state, so hire a lawyer who regularly defends cases in the county or court where you were charged.
ask: How often do you handle cases like mine in this court?
What are the realistic outcomes, and what does each one involve?
Who will actually work on my case, and how will you keep me informed?
How do you bill, and what is included?

faqs.q: What should I do if I am arrested?
faqs.a: You have the right to remain silent and the right to a lawyer. Politely say that you want a lawyer and do not answer questions about the case until you have spoken to one. Do not discuss the matter with others, and do not sign anything you do not understand.

faqs.q: Can I get a public defender?
faqs.a: If you are charged with a crime that could lead to jail and you cannot afford a lawyer, the court will generally appoint one. Many people also choose to hire a private defense lawyer, who may be able to give a case more individual time. Either way, the lawyer's duty to you is the same.

faqs.q: Can criminal charges be reduced or dismissed?
faqs.a: Sometimes. It depends on the evidence, how it was gathered, the facts of the case and the prosecutor's position. A lawyer can tell you what is realistic after reviewing the details.

faqs.q: How do I find a criminal defense lawyer near me?
faqs.a: Choose your state or city on this page to see the criminal defense firms LawDB lists there, with their addresses, phone numbers and the practice areas they handle.

injury.name: Personal Injury
injury.h1: Personal Injury Lawyers in the United States
injury.card: Car accidents, falls and other injuries caused by someone else.
injury.description: When to hire a personal injury lawyer, what they do and what to ask. Then find injury firms by state and city.
injury.lede: A personal injury lawyer helps people who were hurt because of someone else's carelessness, such as in a car or truck accident, a slip and fall, a dog bite or medical negligence. They gather the evidence, deal with the insurance companies and, if a fair settlement is not offered, take the claim to court.
when: You were hurt in an accident that was not your fault.
An insurance company has called you, offered a settlement or asked for a recorded statement.
Your injuries need ongoing treatment or you cannot work.
The other driver has little or no insurance.
You are not sure who is responsible, for example in a fall on someone's property.
does: Explains whether you have a claim and what it may involve.
Collects medical records, photos, police reports and witness accounts.
Handles the insurance adjusters and negotiates a settlement.
Works with doctors and other experts to show the effect of the injury.
Files the lawsuit and represents you at trial if the claim does not settle.
injury.differ: Injury law is mostly state law. Each state sets its own time limit for filing a claim, and these can be short. States also differ in how fault is shared and in how car insurance works, such as no-fault systems. Because deadlines can pass quietly, speak to a local lawyer early, and ask how fees work: many personal injury lawyers are paid only if you recover money, and you should see that agreement in writing.
ask: Do you handle cases like mine, and what have the results been like?
How are you paid, and what costs do I owe if we do not win?
Who will work on my case day to day?
What should I avoid doing or saying while the claim is open?

faqs.q: Should I talk to the other side's insurance company?
faqs.a: You are usually not required to give a recorded statement, and what you say can be used to reduce your claim. Many people speak to a lawyer first. Never sign a release or accept a settlement before you understand how serious your injuries are.

faqs.q: How long do I have to make a claim?
faqs.a: Each state has a time limit, and it can be short. If you wait, you may lose the right to claim at all. A lawyer can tell you which deadline applies to your situation.

faqs.q: How much does a personal injury lawyer cost?
faqs.a: Many handle injury cases on a contingency basis, which means they are paid a share of what you recover and nothing if you do not. Ask for the agreement in writing and ask what case costs are charged on top.

faqs.q: How do I find a personal injury lawyer near me?
faqs.a: Choose your state or city on this page to see the personal injury firms LawDB lists there, with their addresses, phone numbers and the practice areas they handle.

traffic.name: Traffic Tickets
traffic.h1: Traffic Tickets Lawyers in the United States
traffic.card: Speeding, reckless driving and license problems.
traffic.description: When to hire a traffic ticket lawyer, what they do and what to ask. Then find traffic ticket firms by state and city.
traffic.lede: A traffic ticket lawyer helps drivers who have received a citation, such as for speeding, running a light or reckless driving, or who face a license suspension. They look at whether the ticket can be fought or reduced, handle the court for you where the rules allow, and explain how points and insurance could be affected.
when: You received a ticket and are worried about points or your insurance.
You have a commercial driver's license and a violation could affect your job.
You were cited for reckless driving, racing or driving with a suspended license.
You have been told your license may be suspended or revoked.
You have several tickets and want to understand your options.
does: Reviews the ticket and tells you whether it can be challenged or reduced.
Appears in traffic court for you where the local rules allow it.
Negotiates with the prosecutor for a lesser charge.
Explains how points, fines and insurance may be affected.
Helps with license suspension hearings and reinstatement.
traffic.differ: Traffic rules, fines, point systems and procedures are set by each state, and often differ by county or city. Whether you can have a lawyer appear for you, or must attend yourself, depends on where you were cited. Choose a lawyer who regularly handles tickets in that court.
ask: Have you handled tickets in this court before?
What outcomes are realistic for my ticket?
Do I need to attend in person?
What is your fee, and is it fixed?

faqs.q: Is it worth hiring a lawyer for a ticket?
faqs.a: It can be, especially when points, a higher insurance rate, a commercial license or a more serious charge are involved. A lawyer can tell you whether the cost makes sense for your situation.

faqs.q: Will a ticket raise my insurance?
faqs.a: Often it can, depending on the violation and your insurer. Reducing or dismissing the charge may help avoid that. Ask a lawyer what is possible where you were cited.

faqs.q: What happens if I ignore a ticket?
faqs.a: Ignoring a ticket can lead to extra penalties, a warrant or a license suspension in many places. It is better to respond before the deadline on the citation.

faqs.q: How do I find a traffic ticket lawyer near me?
faqs.a: Choose your state or city on this page to see the traffic ticket firms LawDB lists there, with their addresses, phone numbers and the practice areas they handle.

realestate.name: Real Estate
realestate.h1: Real Estate Lawyers in the United States
realestate.card: Buying and selling property, closings, titles and landlord-tenant issues.
realestate.description: When to hire a real estate lawyer, what they do and what to ask. Then find real estate firms by state and city.
realestate.lede: A real estate lawyer helps with the legal side of buying, selling or owning property: reviewing contracts, checking title, handling the closing, and resolving disputes with buyers, sellers, landlords, tenants or neighbors. They can also help with foreclosure, homeowners association disputes and commercial property.
when: You are buying or selling a home and want the contract reviewed.
There is a problem with the title, a lien or a boundary.
A deal is going wrong, for example a buyer or seller backs out.
You are a landlord or a tenant facing a lease dispute or an eviction.
You are facing foreclosure or a dispute with a homeowners association.
does: Reviews and negotiates purchase and sale contracts.
Checks title and deals with liens or other problems.
Handles or oversees the closing and the transfer of ownership.
Advises on leases, evictions and landlord-tenant disputes.
Represents you in property disputes and foreclosure matters.
realestate.differ: Property law is mostly state law, and practices differ. In some states a lawyer normally handles the closing; in others a title or escrow company does and a lawyer is hired mainly for problems. Because of this, ask a local real estate lawyer what is customary and what is worth paying for in your state.
ask: Is a lawyer customary for this kind of transaction here?
What will you review, and what is your fee?
What problems do you see most often with deals like mine?
Can you also handle the closing?

faqs.q: Do I need a lawyer to buy a home?
faqs.a: Not always. It depends on your state and the deal. A lawyer is worth considering for unusual contracts, title problems or a purchase where a lot of money is at stake.

faqs.q: What does a lawyer check on title?
faqs.a: They look for liens, unpaid taxes, easements and other claims on the property, so you know what you are buying and what could surface later.

faqs.q: Can a lawyer help with an eviction?
faqs.a: Yes. Landlords and tenants both use lawyers for evictions and lease disputes, and the rules and timelines are set by state and local law.

faqs.q: How do I find a real estate lawyer near me?
faqs.a: Choose your state or city on this page to see the real estate firms LawDB lists there, with their addresses, phone numbers and the practice areas they handle.

wills.name: Wills, Trusts & Probate
wills.h1: Wills, Trusts & Probate Lawyers in the United States
wills.card: Wills, trusts, powers of attorney and settling an estate.
wills.description: When to hire a wills and estate lawyer, what they do and what to ask. Then find estate planning firms by state and city.
wills.lede: A wills and estate lawyer helps you plan for what happens to your property, and who decides for you if you cannot, and helps families settle an estate after someone dies. That includes wills, living trusts, powers of attorney, health care directives, guardianship and probate.
when: You want a will or trust, or your family situation has changed.
You need a power of attorney or a health care directive.
A loved one has died and you need to settle their estate (probate).
You are worried about care costs, or about a family member who cannot manage their affairs.
You own property in more than one state.
does: Prepares wills, living trusts and powers of attorney.
Advises on how to avoid probate and plan for taxes where it applies.
Guides executors and families through probate.
Helps set up guardianship or arrangements for a loved one.
Represents you if an estate or a will is disputed.
wills.differ: Estate law is mostly state law. Rules on what makes a will valid, how probate works and how long it takes differ by state, and property in another state may need its own process. Choose a lawyer who practices estate law in the state where you live or where the estate is being settled.
ask: How much of your practice is estate planning or probate?
Would a will or a trust suit my situation, and why?
What is your fee, and is it fixed or hourly?
What documents should I bring?

faqs.q: Do I need a will if I have little property?
faqs.a: A will lets you say who gets what and who looks after any children, and without one state law decides. Even with modest assets, many people find it worthwhile. A lawyer can tell you what suits your situation.

faqs.q: What is probate?
faqs.a: Probate is the court process of confirming a will, paying debts and passing assets to the people entitled to them. How it works, and how long it takes, depends on the state.

faqs.q: Do I need a trust as well as a will?
faqs.a: Sometimes. A trust can help manage assets, plan for incapacity or avoid probate for some property. Whether it suits you depends on your assets, family and state.

faqs.q: How do I find a wills and estate lawyer near me?
faqs.a: Choose your state or city on this page to see the estate planning and probate firms LawDB lists there, with their addresses, phone numbers and the practice areas they handle.

business.name: Business & Corporate
business.h1: Business & Corporate Lawyers in the United States
business.card: Starting, running, buying and selling a business.
business.description: When to hire a business lawyer, what they do and what to ask. Then find business law firms by state and city.
business.lede: A business lawyer helps owners set up and run a company on a sound legal footing: choosing a structure such as an LLC or corporation, writing and reviewing contracts, protecting the business and handling disputes. They also advise on partnerships, hiring, buying and selling a business and day-to-day compliance.
when: You are starting a business and choosing a legal structure.
You are signing or writing contracts with customers, suppliers or partners.
Co-owners need a written agreement about ownership and what happens if one leaves.
You are buying, selling or raising money for a business.
A partner, customer or employee is in dispute with the company.
does: Helps form an LLC, corporation or partnership and keeps it in good standing.
Drafts and reviews contracts and agreements.
Advises on partnership, shareholder and operating agreements.
Supports the purchase or sale of a business.
Represents the business in disputes and negotiations.
business.differ: Companies are created under state law, and the state where you form the company matters. Licensing, taxes and some regulations also depend on where you operate, and federal rules apply in areas such as employment and taxes. A local business lawyer can explain which rules apply to your company.
ask: Have you worked with businesses like mine?
What do you recommend for structure, and why?
How do you bill for ongoing advice?
What should I put in writing before we start?

faqs.q: Should I form an LLC or a corporation?
faqs.a: It depends on your goals, the number of owners, how you plan to raise money and how you want to be taxed. A business lawyer, often together with an accountant, can help you choose.

faqs.q: Why do I need a written agreement with my partners?
faqs.a: A clear agreement says who owns what, who decides, and what happens if someone leaves or the partners disagree. It is far easier to agree on these points at the start than during a dispute.

faqs.q: Can a lawyer review a contract before I sign?
faqs.a: Yes, and it is a common reason to hire one. A lawyer can point out risks and terms you may want to change before you are bound by them.

faqs.q: How do I find a business lawyer near me?
faqs.a: Choose your state or city on this page to see the business firms LawDB lists there, with their addresses, phone numbers and the practice areas they handle.

employment.name: Employment
employment.h1: Employment Lawyers in the United States
employment.card: Firing, discrimination, unpaid wages and workplace disputes.
employment.description: When to hire an employment lawyer, what they do and what to ask. Then find employment firms by state and city.
employment.lede: An employment lawyer helps workers and employers with problems at work: being fired, discrimination or harassment, unpaid wages and overtime, retaliation, leave rights, employment contracts and non-compete agreements. They explain your rights and options and, where needed, take a case to an agency or a court.
when: You were fired, laid off or pushed to resign and think it may not have been lawful.
You face discrimination, harassment or retaliation at work.
You are owed wages, overtime or other pay.
You were offered a severance package or a non-compete agreement and want it reviewed.
You are an employer facing a complaint or writing policies.
does: Reviews your situation and explains your rights under federal and state law.
Negotiates severance, settlements and contract terms.
Files complaints with the right agency when required.
Represents you in a lawsuit or in arbitration.
Advises employers on compliance and handling complaints.
employment.differ: Workplace rights come from both federal law and state law, and states often give more protection than the federal rules. Most states treat employment as at will, with important exceptions, and some complaints must first go to an agency with its own short deadlines. A lawyer in your state can tell you which rules and deadlines apply.
ask: How much of your work is employment law, and do you represent employees, employers or both?
What deadlines apply to my situation?
How are you paid, and is there a free first meeting?
What documents should I collect now?

faqs.q: Can my employer fire me for any reason?
faqs.a: In most states employment is at will, which means an employer can end it without notice. There are important exceptions, such as discrimination, retaliation, and rights under a contract. A lawyer can tell you whether an exception may apply.

faqs.q: What should I do if I think I am being discriminated against?
faqs.a: Keep a record of what happened, with dates, names and any messages, and speak to a lawyer. Some claims must be filed with a government agency within a short time.

faqs.q: Should I sign a severance agreement right away?
faqs.a: Not necessarily. These agreements often waive your right to bring claims, so it is worth having a lawyer review the terms and, where possible, negotiate before you sign.

faqs.q: How do I find a employment lawyer near me?
faqs.a: Choose your state or city on this page to see the employment firms LawDB lists there, with their addresses, phone numbers and the practice areas they handle.

immigration.name: Immigration
immigration.h1: Immigration Lawyers in the United States
immigration.card: Visas, green cards, citizenship and removal defense.
immigration.description: When to hire an immigration lawyer, what they do and what to ask. Then find immigration firms by state and city.
immigration.lede: An immigration lawyer helps people with the legal process of coming to, staying in or becoming a citizen of the United States: family-based and employment-based visas, green cards, work permits, citizenship, asylum and defending against removal (deportation). They prepare applications, represent you with the immigration agencies and appear in immigration court.
when: You want to sponsor a family member or apply for a green card.
You or an employer need a work visa or a change of status.
You are applying for citizenship.
You have received a notice from an immigration agency or from immigration court.
You or a family member face detention or removal proceedings.
does: Explains which immigration options you may qualify for.
Prepares and files applications and responds to agency requests.
Represents you at interviews and in immigration court.
Advises on how past events, such as a criminal charge, may affect your case.
Helps employers sponsor workers.
immigration.differ: Immigration is governed by federal law, so a lawyer in any state can generally handle your case, but experience with your local immigration court and office can help. Only licensed attorneys, or specially accredited representatives, may give legal advice on immigration. Be careful with anyone who is not, including "notarios" and consultants, because mistakes can be hard to undo.
ask: Are you a licensed attorney, and do you handle my kind of case?
What are my realistic options, and what are the risks?
What will the process cost, including government fees?
What happens if the case is denied?

faqs.q: Can I file immigration forms myself?
faqs.a: Many people do, but errors and missing information can cause delays or denials, and some situations are risky to file without advice. A lawyer is worth considering when your history is complicated.

faqs.q: How do I know my immigration helper is a real lawyer?
faqs.a: Ask for their bar number and check it with the state bar. Only attorneys and accredited representatives may give immigration legal advice, and anyone who promises a guaranteed result should be treated with caution.

faqs.q: What should I do if I receive a notice to appear in court?
faqs.a: Do not ignore it. Missing a hearing can lead to an order of removal. Speak to an immigration lawyer as soon as possible and bring the notice with you.

faqs.q: How do I find a immigration lawyer near me?
faqs.a: Choose your state or city on this page to see the immigration firms LawDB lists there, with their addresses, phone numbers and the practice areas they handle.

litigation.name: Civil Litigation
litigation.h1: Civil Litigation Lawyers in the United States
litigation.card: Lawsuits, contract disputes and getting a fair result in court.
litigation.description: When to hire a civil litigation lawyer, what they do and what to ask. Then find litigation firms by state and city.
litigation.lede: A civil litigation lawyer represents people and businesses in disputes that go to court, such as contract disagreements, property disputes, business and partnership conflicts and claims for money owed. They assess the case, try to settle it where that makes sense, and take it through the court process if it does not.
when: You have been sued or received a demand letter.
Someone owes you money or has not honored a contract.
A dispute with a business partner, neighbor or contractor is getting serious.
You want to know whether your claim is worth pursuing.
You are told you must respond to a lawsuit by a certain date.
does: Reviews your documents and explains your position.
Sends demand letters and negotiates settlements.
Handles mediation and arbitration.
Files and defends lawsuits and represents you at trial.
Advises on the costs and risks before you decide how far to go.
litigation.differ: Civil cases are heard in state courts or federal courts, depending on the parties and the type of claim, and each state has its own procedures, deadlines and small claims rules. Lawsuits are expensive and slow, so a good lawyer will tell you early what the case is likely to cost and whether a settlement makes sense.
ask: What do you think my case is worth, and what are the risks?
How do you charge, and what are the likely costs through trial?
Is mediation or settlement realistic here?
How long might this take?

faqs.q: What should I do if I am served with a lawsuit?
faqs.a: Do not ignore it. There is a deadline to respond, and missing it can lead to a judgment against you. Speak to a lawyer promptly and keep all the papers.

faqs.q: Do I need a lawyer for small claims court?
faqs.a: Usually not, since small claims courts are designed for people to represent themselves. For larger or more complicated disputes, a lawyer can be worth the cost.

faqs.q: Can a dispute be settled without going to trial?
faqs.a: Yes, and most are. Settlement, mediation and arbitration are common because they are faster and cheaper than a trial, and a lawyer can advise on when they make sense.

faqs.q: How do I find a civil litigation lawyer near me?
faqs.a: Choose your state or city on this page to see the civil litigation firms LawDB lists there, with their addresses, phone numbers and the practice areas they handle.
